para.verbatim:
embed:rst Keeps only the lines (vertices) whose decoded data satisfies 'predicate', dropping the rest :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Where :cpp:func:`fix` maps every line through its filters and keeps them all, this *selects* -- the lines it keeps come through byte for byte :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` .. note:: A kept line's **original bytes are copied through untouched** rather than being re-encoded from its decoded data, so a lossy data type (a :cpp:class:`BufUnorm`, a :cpp:class:`BufFloat16`) cannot be perturbed by the decode a predicate needs. Only which lines survive is up to the predicate, never their contents .. note:: A ``.buf`` file has no idea which of its lines is which vertex, so dropping lines out of a ``.vb`` invalidates every index in the ``.ib`` that pointed past them. The returned line indices are exactly what remapping those indices needs -- see :cpp:class:`IbFile` :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` If 'predicate' throws, the file is left completely untouched -- nothing is written until every line has been decided

parameterdescription.para: Decides whether one line is kept, given that line's decoded data

simplesect.para: The indices of the lines that were kept, in ascending order. Empty when nothing was kept, and also when the file has no elements to decode by

parameterdescription.para: if the kept bytes do not divide evenly into lines only reachable when this file's own data was not a whole number of lines to start with

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Decodes the whole file at once, **column by column** rather than line by line -- the bulk counterpart to :cpp:func:`decodeLine` :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Where :cpp:func:`decodeLine` builds a fresh keyed map per line, this walks the elements in declaration order and writes straight into one contiguous, uniformly typed buffer per column, so nothing is hashed, allocated or boxed per line. That is what makes it the right shape to hand to a columnar consumer (a ``numpy`` array, a dataframe, a column store) -- see the ``BufTools`` Python-side tools built on it :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` The columns come back in **declaration order** (element by element, then data type within each element), not sorted by element key -- a caller wanting some other order sorts what it gets back

simplesect.para: One entry per column, each holding one value per line. Empty when the file has no elements

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Every line's values for one element, as integers in line order -- ``out[line][i]`` is the element's ``i``-th data type :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` The row-shaped counterpart to :cpp:func:`decodeAll`, for a caller that works a vertex at a time: a `blend`_ buffer's ids or weights, or an index buffer's triangles

parameterdescription.para: The element to take, eg. :cpp:member:BlendFile::BlendIndicesKey

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Merges several other ``.buf`` files into this one, line by line :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A GI character's vertex buffer does not live in one file -- it is split across a ``Position.buf``, a ``Blend.buf`` and a ``Texcoord.buf``, one line each per vertex. This stitches such a set back together: line *i* of the result is line *i* of every source, concatenated in the order given, and this file's #getElements becomes every source's elements in that same order (deep-copied, so the sources stay usable) :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` The number of lines produced is the **smallest** line count among the sources, so a ragged set truncates rather than reading past the end of the shortest file. A null source is skipped

parameterdescription.para: The .buf files to merge, in the byte order their elements should appear in a line
if the merged bytes do not divide evenly into lines (only reachable when a source's own data was not a whole number of lines)

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Appends every line of several other ``.buf`` files onto the end of this one :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` The **vertical** counterpart to :cpp:func:`merge`: where that one widens a line by concatenating a matching line out of each source, this one *lengthens* the file, so the result holds this file's lines followed by each source's lines in the order given :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Each source's elements must be a **superset** of this file's -- for every one of this file's elements, the source must carry an element with the same key (see #getElements) and the same :cpp:class:`BufDataType`\\s. The source may carry as many further elements as it likes, and in any order; those are simply dropped, and each appended line is rebuilt in **this** file's element order. So a full ``.vb`` can be appended onto a ``Position.buf`` and contributes only its positions :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` .. note:: Only the data types have to match, not :cpp:func:`BufElementType::getFormatName` -- the format name is 3dmigoto's label for a layout, and two elements spelling it differently still occupy the same bytes .. note:: A matched element's bytes are copied straight across rather than decoded and re-encoded, so nothing an appended value goes through can perturb it :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Every source is checked against this file **before** any byte is copied, so a source that breaks the superset rule leaves this file exactly as it was rather than partly appended to. A null source is skipped, and a source is allowed to be this file itself

parameterdescription.para: The .buf files whose lines to append, in the order they should appear after this file's own lines
if a source is missing one of this file's elements, or carries it with different data types
if the appended bytes do not divide evenly into lines (only reachable when this file's own data was not a whole number of lines)

memberdef.name: restride

para.verbatim:
embed:rst This file's lines rewritten in another layout -- another stride -- element by element :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Two skins of a character can read one buffer in different layouts: Miyabi's Body ``Texcoord.buf`` is 24 bytes a vertex (``COLOR``, ``TEXCOORD0`` to ``TEXCOORD3``) where her skin's Dress reads 20 (no ``TEXCOORD3``). Each element of 'toElements' is filled, line by line, from: #. this file's element of the same name, byte for byte; #. otherwise this file's element named by 'fillFrom' for it (``TEXCOORD3`` from ``TEXCOORD0``), byte for byte; #. otherwise zeros. An element of this file that 'toElements' does not name is dropped. Nothing is decoded, so no value can be perturbed on the way

parameterdescription.para: The layout to write, in byte order
For an element of 'toElements' this file does not have, the name of this file's element to copy into it. Default: none

simplesect.para: The rewritten bytes, one line of 'toElements' per line of this file

parameterdescription.para: if an element copied across is not the same size on both sides

para.verbatim:
embed:rst The **data** section of the dump text for this ``.buf`` file -- the text a 3dmigoto frame analysis writes, which `Blender`_ can then import :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` One line per element per line (vertex), in the elements' declared order, shaped as ``prefix[lineInd]+byteOffset elementKey: value, value, ...``, with a blank line between lines. Deliberately only the data: a complete dump also needs a header, and that header differs by the kind of buffer being dumped :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` .. note:: Every number is formatted exactly the way `Python`_'s ``str`` would format it -- shortest round-trip for a `floating point`_ value, and `Python`_'s own choice between fixed and scientific notation. That is not cosmetic: it keeps the output byte identical to what a real frame analysis writes

parameterdescription.para: The buffer name each entry is prefixed with the vertex buffer slot a real dump was taken from

simplesect.para: The data section of the dump text. Empty when the file has no lines

para.verbatim:
embed:rst The **data** section of the dump text in an *index buffer*'s flat form -- every one of a line's values on one line, separated by 'valueSep', with no element name or byte offset :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` This is what a ``.ib`` file's dump looks like (``0 1 2`` per triangular face), as opposed to the per-element form :cpp:func:`getDumpStr` produces for a vertex buffer

parameterdescription.para: What to put between two values on the same line

simplesect.para: The data section of the dump text. Empty when the file has no lines

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Reads dump text back into this file's bytes -- the inverse of :cpp:func:`getDumpStr` :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` The values are encoded with this file's **current** #getElements, one text line per element and one blank-line-separated block per line (vertex), so a round trip through :cpp:func:`getDumpStr` and back returns the bytes it started with :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A complete dump file works too, not just the data section :cpp:func:`getDumpStr` returns: anything up to and including a ``vertex-data:`` marker is skipped. Each line's values are taken from after its last ``:``, so the ``prefix[i]+offset elementKey:`` part is ignored rather than having to match :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A block with fewer values than the elements need is zero-filled and extra values are dropped, so every block always contributes exactly #getBytesPerLine bytes

parameterdescription.para: The dump text to read
if the encoded bytes do not divide evenly into lines

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Reads *index buffer* dump text back into this file's bytes -- the inverse of :cpp:func:`getFlatDumpStr` :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` One text line per line of the file, its values separated by 'valueSep'. A complete dump file works too: a header line is recognised by containing a ``:`` (every line of a ``.ib`` dump's header does, and none of its data lines do) and skipped

parameterdescription.para: The dump text to read
What separates two values on the same line

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Encodes whole columns back into the file's bytes -- the inverse of :cpp:func:`decodeAll`, and the bulk counterpart to :cpp:func:`encodeLine` :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` The columns are matched to the file's current #getElements by their :cpp:member:`BufColumnData::elementKey`/:cpp:member:`BufColumnData::valueInd`, so their order in 'columns' does not matter; a column the file has no data type for is ignored, and a data type with no matching column encodes as 0. The number of lines produced is the longest column's length :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` This sets #getSrc to the newly encoded bytes and re-reads from it, so the usual :cpp:func:`read` validation applies

if the encoded bytes do not divide evenly into lines for the file's current getElements

embed:rst Every line's value for one single :cpp:class:`BufDataType` within one element, laid out contiguously -- one entry per line, all of the same type :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Which of the three alternatives a column uses is decided by the :cpp:class:`BufDataType` it belongs to, never by the bytes: a signed integer type always yields ``long long``, an unsigned one ``unsigned long long`` and a `floating point`_ one ``double``, exactly matching the alternative that type's :cpp:func:`BufDataType::decode` returns

embed:rst This class inherits from :cpp:class:`BufFile` :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Used for handling ``Texcoord.buf`` files: one element of UV values a vertex (:cpp:member:`uvElement`), whose first two values are the vertex's U and V, beside any others the layout declares :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A mod's UVs can carry two things a draw does not expect: a value that is not a number, and a U past ``1`` that relies on the sampler WRAPPING -- a part UV'd into the ``[1, 2)`` tile. #clean sets the first to ``0`` and folds the second back into ``[0, 1)``, which selects the same texel wherever the pass wraps and keeps the part right where it does not
